route: Passive handheld UMI gripper with robot-mounted compatible camera/gripper
official_bom_or_hardware_guide: Official GitHub links to Google Hardware Guide and Onshape; paper reports low-cost gripper and camera accessories
key_bom_items: 3D-printed PLA/TPU parallel gripper; MGN9C linear rails; M3 screws/nuts; compression springs; ArUco tags; GoPro HERO9 with Max Lens Mod; GoPro Labs firmware; robot-side UR5/Franka + WSG-50 style deployment mount
license_status: Software repo MIT. Hardware guide is public but Google Doc export needs manual verification. Third-party mechanism/finger designs are acknowledged in repo; keep attribution and verify CAD/license before commercial reuse.
critical_sensor_availability: GoPro HERO9/Max Lens Mod is a legacy consumer-camera stack; exact model supply should not be assumed. Main technical dependency is extracting reliable video + IMU for ORB-SLAM3 and preserving timestamps.
china_localization_ideas: Keep geometry and data interface, localize parts: domestic 3D printing/CNC; domestic MGN rails/springs/screws; DJI Osmo Action/Insta360 Ace or industrial fisheye camera + external IMU as camera substitute after calibration; JAKA/Dobot/Aubo/UR/xArm robot-side mounts; Robotiq/DH/Agile Robots/WEISS-like gripper adapters.
discontinuation_or_supply_risk: Medium: exact GoPro HERO9/Max Lens Mod and WSG-50 setup may be harder to standardize in China; ORB-SLAM3 pipeline is fragile in weak texture/occlusion.
v0_productization_suggestion: Use as v0 baseline: one passive gripper SKU + one camera SKU + calibration board + standard Zarr exporter. Sell data package, QC report and baseline training, not only hardware.
research_status: BOM partly verified from official repo/project and prior raw extract; exact Google Doc links require manual browser review.

route: Plug-and-play UMI redesign using commercial pose tracker
official_bom_or_hardware_guide: Project page and FastUMI_Data repo provide data collection code; web page links hardware 3D printing/purchase and installation; repo documents T265/GoPro workflow
key_bom_items: Handheld and robot-mounted decoupled device; GoPro fisheye RGB; Intel RealSense T265 for pose; ArUco gripper width markers; ROS Noetic; HDF5 and Zarr conversion scripts; FastUMI Pro adds tactile fingertip and RoboBaton Mini replacement
license_status: FastUMI_Data repo MIT. Hardware CAD/purchase artifacts appear public on project page but per-file hardware license needs verification.
critical_sensor_availability: T265 is end-of-life and not supported in later librealsense versions; repo recommends librealsense v2.53.1. RoboBaton Mini is a Chinese VIO-SLAM replacement candidate, with vendor pages showing Mini product/downloads and domestic distributor availability.
china_localization_ideas: For China v0, skip T265 stockpiling and design around RoboBaton Mini or another domestic VIO module. Keep a tracker abstraction layer: pose source can be T265, RoboBaton, ARKit, Vive, LiDAR-SLAM or motion capture.
discontinuation_or_supply_risk: High if relying on T265. Medium if RoboBaton Mini API/SDK stability and calibration accuracy are not tested across manipulation occlusions.
v0_productization_suggestion: Productize as the first practical kit: handheld collector + robot-side mount + pose-source abstraction + HDF5/Zarr/LeRobot export + RViz-like live QC. Offer T265-compatible import only for legacy customers.
research_status: Verified repo license and workflow; hardware purchase list details still need manual project-page artifact review.

route: UMI extension with low-cost LiDAR-centric SLAM
official_bom_or_hardware_guide: UMI-3D Hardware repo has explicit BOM, CAD/STL links, wiring, ROS driver, and target cost
key_bom_items: Livox MID-360/MID-360S; Hikrobot MV-CB013-A0UC-S camera; ZLKC MTV185IR12MP lens; LiDAR-camera hardware synchronizer; 12V battery; PLA/TPU printed gripper; ARX L5/R5/X5 and Agilex Piper mounts
license_status: UMI-3D-Hardware repo Apache-2.0. SLAM/data pipeline repo license should be checked per repository before redistribution.
critical_sensor_availability: Very favorable for China: Livox, Hikrobot and ZLKC are China-accessible components; project page claims total cost under RMB 5000 / USD 700.
china_localization_ideas: This is the strongest domestic localization route: use Livox/Hikrobot/ZLKC as default; replace Taobao sync board with in-house trigger/sync PCB for reliability; package ROS Noetic driver and calibration SOP.
discontinuation_or_supply_risk: Low-to-medium: component supply looks local, but MID-360 price/availability and synchronizer quality need procurement confirmation. Technical risk shifts from supply to calibration and LiDAR-camera synchronization.
v0_productization_suggestion: Make v1 rugged kit around UMI-3D for weak-texture industrial/retail scenes. Differentiate with one-click rosbag recording, calibration validation, point-cloud replay and SLAM success-rate report.

route: Multimodal tactile/force/pose UMI for contact-rich tasks
official_bom_or_hardware_guide: Project page and paper describe hardware design; public GitHub/BOM not found during this pass
key_bom_items: Compact robot-compatible handheld gripper; ViTac tactile sensors on fingertips; 6D force-torque sensor; Vive tracker; continuous self-locking mechanism; synchronized visual/tactile/force/pose streams
license_status: License unknown. No official public code or hardware repo found in this pass.
critical_sensor_availability: Vive tracker is commercially available but needs Lighthouse/SteamVR infrastructure. ViTac and 6D F/T sensor supply, price and licensing are not yet verified.
china_localization_ideas: Use as premium module inspiration, not v0: domestic tactile options include GelSight-like optical tactile modules, 9DTact-like sensors, DIGIT-like modules, or custom silicone+camera tactile fingertips; domestic F/T sensor vendors and ATI/OnRobot/Robotiq alternatives need vendor testing.
discontinuation_or_supply_risk: High: no public BOM/license; tactile/force sensors are costly, fragile and calibration-heavy; Vive tracker may be awkward for industrial ToB deployment.
v0_productization_suggestion: Do not commercialize first. Use TacUMI ideas for vertical pilots: cable routing, insertion, wiping, polishing. Deliver multimodal segmentation labels and contact event tags as premium data add-on.
research_status: Needs follow-up: identify ViTac vendor/repo, F/T sensor model, tracker model, and licensing.

route: Force-aware compliant UMI using CoinFT and iPhone ARKit
official_bom_or_hardware_guide: UMI-FT site links official hardware guide; UMI-FT repo gives data collection/processing folder structures and Zarr fields
key_bom_items: iPhone 15 Pro or ARKit iPhone; two CoinFT six-axis F/T sensors; Teensy 4.0; breadboard/wires/connectors; PLA/TPU printed gripper; optional contact mic; grip tape; M2/M3 screws; UR robot + WSG gripper for deployment
license_status: UMI-FT repo MIT. CoinFT project is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and explicitly disallows commercial use without separate Stanford license; this is a major commercialization constraint.
critical_sensor_availability: CoinFT is a research sensor, material cost is low but commercial supply is not established. Hardware guide warns about power fluctuation sensitivity, warm-up drift and mounting-induced PCB warping.
china_localization_ideas: For China commercialization, do not embed CoinFT without license. Build a replaceable force module: domestic 6-axis F/T sensor for robot-side; lower-cost strain gauge/capacitive fingertip prototype; ARKit/iPhone route can be localized only if iPhone supply/app policy is acceptable.
discontinuation_or_supply_risk: High for CoinFT commercial license and production yield. Medium for iPhone/ARKit dependency if targeting domestic enterprise procurement.
v0_productization_suggestion: Treat UMI-FT as a high-value roadmap item after passive/vio kit works. Productize force data as service: force calibration certificate, drift report, compliance labels and contact-force safety limits.

route: Multi-view UMI for cross-embodiment scene context
official_bom_or_hardware_guide: Project site describes mechanical design and says code/hardware repository coming soon
key_bom_items: Handheld modular gripper; robot-mounted three-jaw gripper configuration; modified two-gripper UMI with affordable linear motors; egocentric camera plus third-person camera; segmentation/inpainting-style processed view
license_status: Website CC BY-SA 4.0. Code and hardware repository marked coming soon; hardware/software license unknown.
critical_sensor_availability: Sensors are ordinary cameras and motors in principle, but exact camera/motor/BOM are not published. Main dependency is robust multi-view calibration and human/robot visual-domain processing.
china_localization_ideas: Easy to localize if BOM appears: domestic USB/industrial cameras, Hikrobot/Daheng/MindVision, low-cost linear actuators, fixed tripod/overhead rigs. For ToB, pair with UMI/FastUMI/UMI-3D kit instead of standalone.
discontinuation_or_supply_risk: Medium: not blocked by rare sensor, but blocked by missing public implementation artifacts.
v0_productization_suggestion: Use as service add-on for large workspaces: shelf replenishment, warehouse totes, retail display, lab bench. Bundle third-person calibration board and automatic view-quality check.

official_bom_or_hardware_guide: Official GitHub README includes BoM, 3D printing settings, assembly guide and license
key_bom_items: DYNAMIXEL XL430-W250-T; ROBOTIS U2D2; U2D2 power hub; constant-force springs; MGN7C 80mm linear rail/carriage; flat belt; heat-set inserts; M2/M3 screws; PLA printed body; optional TPU fingers using UMI settings
license_status: MIT, with third-party UMI content under MIT according to repo.
critical_sensor_availability: Dynamixel and U2D2 are globally available but can be expensive; MGN rails/springs/belts are easy to source in China.
china_localization_ideas: Domestic substitutions: Feetech/Hiwonder/serial-bus servo for Dynamixel after torque/backlash tests; local MGN7C rails; CNC/PA-CF printed body; custom PCB replacing U2D2/power hub if volume grows.
discontinuation_or_supply_risk: Low-to-medium: supply manageable, but servo substitution changes control fidelity and reliability.
v0_productization_suggestion: Good robot-side v0 gripper reference. Use for deployment mirror of passive UMI data; package with current limit, emergency open, overload logging and replaceable fingertips.

official_bom_or_hardware_guide: GELLO mechanical/software repos and project page; BOM assembly instructions in Google Doc
key_bom_items: Per-robot 3D-printed kinematic leader arm; off-the-shelf motors; shared gripper parts; supported designs for Franka, UR5, xArm7, YAM, Lite6, AR4, FR3/FR3 Duo; U2D2/serial setup in software
license_status: Software repo MIT; mechanical repo MIT; website CC BY-SA 4.0.
critical_sensor_availability: No rare sensor. Main dependencies are motors, printed parts, controller electronics and target robot availability.
china_localization_ideas: Highly localizable: adapt to JAKA/Dobot/Aubo/Elite/xArm/ARX/Piper using local motor kits and CNC/3D printing. Strong fit for customers who already own target arms.
discontinuation_or_supply_risk: Low supply risk; medium engineering risk per new robot kinematic replica and calibration.
v0_productization_suggestion: Offer as ToB data service option when client has robot arms and needs high-quality robot-native trajectories. Pair with UMI-like data for out-of-lab scene coverage.
research_status: Good control group and near-term service route.

route: Bimanual and mobile robot-native data collection
official_bom_or_hardware_guide: Official ALOHA and Mobile ALOHA repos link hardware assembly tutorials; project sites describe system and cost
key_bom_items: Four Interbotix/X-series arms for stationary ALOHA; four cameras; ROS Noetic; USB3-heavy workstation; Mobile ALOHA adds mobile base and whole-body teleoperation; ACT training stack; HDF5 data episodes
license_status: ALOHA repo MIT; Mobile ALOHA repo MIT. Hardware kit terms and Google hardware tutorial details need vendor/legal review.
critical_sensor_availability: Commercial components are available but full system is expensive, bulky and robot-dependent. USB stability, camera sync and multi-robot maintenance are operational bottlenecks.
china_localization_ideas: Domestic route: replace Interbotix arms with xArm Lite/ARX/Piper/Dobot/JAKA small arms; use domestic RGB cameras; local mobile base; use LeRobot/ACT compatible dataset export. Build service cell rather than handheld kit.
discontinuation_or_supply_risk: Medium: not discontinued but cost, import lead time and maintenance burden are high.
v0_productization_suggestion: Use as high-end data-factory reference for bimanual/mobile tasks. Do not lead with it for low-cost entry; use when client specifically needs robot-native dual-arm/mobile data.
